clue.text: Support letters after appointment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an upright pole that holds something up
second meaning: the mail delivered to a house

explanation.surface: Someone writes letters backing a candidate after they have been given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has more meanings than two here: 'after' is its Latin sense as a prefix, and an appointment is a job, also this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden upright holding a fence is one sense; the mail delivered by carriers is the other, common in British usage.

clue.text: Some robes evidently far too heavy

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, so a run inside the words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Certain gowns are plainly much too heavy to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside rOBES Evidently.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity describes a body weight well beyond what is healthy, the medical term for excess fat.

clue.text: Reptiles, huge nuisance for cat

parts.note: slow shelled reptiles
something that is hell is a great torment

explanation.surface: Some reptiles are a real menace to a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge nuisance' is a fair stretch for hell, as in 'the neighbours are hell'; 'for' merely links the wordplay to the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat whose mottled black, orange and brown coat resembles the reptile's shell.

clue.text: Birds wrangle with noisy arguments

parts.note: to spar is to argue or quarrel
a row, rhyming with cow, is a loud quarrel

explanation.surface: Birds squabble among themselves with loud quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWS here is the British word for loud quarrels, not lines of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparrows are small brown songbirds, an example of the class of feathered creatures named.

clue.text: Splashed front of parka in river mud

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: silt is the fine mud a river deposits

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the coat

explanation.surface: Someone's parka got splashed at the front while wading in a muddy river.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside SILT after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that has been spilt has been slopped over the edge, splashing about, past tense of the verb.

clue.text: A rugby player's eating nothing suitable

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: A plus PROP'S: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A rugby player is off his food, eating nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S of 'player's' supplies the final S; O slips in just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means fitting or pertinent to the occasion, borrowed from French 'à propos', to the purpose.

clue.text: New form of an incinerator following refurbishment

indicators.note: a refurbished thing has been taken apart and rebuilt, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A council's rebuilt incinerator comes back in a new design.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder needs the 'an' as well as 'incinerator' to make thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is rebirth of a soul in another body, so it is a fresh bodily shape, figuratively any revival.

clue.text: Why candle almost out in Irish town?

parts.note: the wick is the burning part of a candle
a flame nearly out is burning low

explanation.surface: A puzzled visitor asks why the candles are guttering in an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The question has a joke answer: why is the candle almost out? Because its WICK is LOW. Wicklow is a town south of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicklow is a coastal town on Ireland's east coast, also giving its name to a county and mountains.

clue.text: More enthusiastic man painting? That is right

parts.note: a man is a he
painting is a form of art
i.e. abbreviates Latin id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A painter gets keener on his work, and someone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is right' reads as a comment on the question, but it is two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty describes warm, vigorous, wholehearted feeling, so the comparative form means showing greater zeal.

clue.text: Creep along in church

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run through 'in church' is a coincidence, as the setter uses the abbreviation
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes slowly down the aisle of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placement word but is kept as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move forward by very small steps, slowly and carefully, the verb from the unit of length.

clue.text: In two brief months, boil

parts.note: the short form of December, the first of the pair
the short form of October, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Within a couple of short months, something comes to the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' tells you to shorten the months to their calendar abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoct is to extract a substance's essence by boiling it down in water, a chemist's or cook's verb.

clue.text: Ultimately unsuited to cycling, one walked

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so each word gives only its closing letter

parts.note: closing letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone unfit for riding a bike simply went on foot instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like an instruction to rotate letters, but it is only one of the three words whose endings are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hound is taken out on a lead every day, so it is the creature typically exercised this way.

clue.text: Preserved vegetables for cheeky child

definitions.meaning: first meaning: vegetables kept in vinegar or brine

explanation.surface: Jarred vegetables are served to a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a mischievous child a 'little pickle' is British and affectionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutney-like relish of vinegar-soaked produce is one sense; an impish, naughty youngster is the informal British other.

clue.text: Terrible war starts — a GP's to seek desperate salvation

indicators.note: something terrible is a dreadful mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A dreadful war breaks out, and a family doctor is left hunting for any way out.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain; the letters come in handy as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a drowning person clutching floating stalks: trying anything, however hopeless, to be rescued.

clue.text: Free to take another contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to let go, set at liberty

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as RE-LEASE, renting the property once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting a prisoner go is one sense; signing a fresh rental agreement on a flat is the hyphenated other.

clue.text: Degenerate American going to pot

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a pot is slang for a sporting cup or prize

explanation.surface: A worthless American is going to seed, taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pot' is an idiom for decline, but 'pot' here is the silverware won in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles that waste away through disuse wither, so as a verb it means decline or deteriorate physically.

clue.text: Aristocrat turning up conceals title

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upward means reading from the bottom to the top
what a word conceals is tucked inside it, so the letters are found within

parts.note: the second to fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A nobleman shows up hiding what rank he holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aristocrat' wants to be the definition; the rank is at the other end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the honorific given to a knight or baronet, prefixed to the name, a form of address.

clue.text: Charlie no winner, but not so far behind

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
someone who did not win

explanation.surface: Charlie didn't win the race, but trailed the leader by only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie reads as a runner's name; it is the phonetic alphabet's C.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nearer to someone ahead means the gap is smaller, the comparative of near in distance.

clue.text: Friend beginning to recover after earth tremor

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the piece named first is placed second

parts.note: an earthquake, shortened

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: A friend begins to get better after an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital-F Friend is the crossword's way to a member of the Religious Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, and call each other by that name.

clue.text: Almost strange name for band

indicators.note: almost all of something means it stops just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: QUEER, odd, without its last letter
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone thinks up a rather odd name for their group.
explanation.walkthrough: The band is the rock group fronted by Freddie Mercury.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen is the British rock group of Freddie Mercury and Brian May, famous for Bohemian Rhapsody.

clue.text: Perfect climbing over base of Everest, go up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: pure means flawless

indicators.note: the base of a word in a down clue is its bottom, final letter

parts.note: final letter of the mountain

explanation.surface: A perfect ascent begins at Everest's foot: shall we climb?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the reversed word above the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that erupts blows its top, sending lava and ash skyward, which is a question-marked sense of rising.

clue.text: Pheasant, for example, unable to walk properly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wild birds hunted for sport and food

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is old-fashioned British: a 'game leg' is an injured, limping one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot wild fowl like grouse and partridge form one sense; an old adjective meaning lame or crippled is the other.

clue.text: Beloved park in holy surroundings

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: pious means devout; 'surroundings' says it wraps round
a rec is a recreation ground, a British public park

explanation.surface: A cherished park lies within sacred grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'park' reads as the obvious P abbreviation, but it gives the British REC, a recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precious is dearly treasured and held in great affection, highly valued by its owner.

clue.text: Methodist's awful news about destruction of Yale

indicators.note: to be about something is to go around it, enclosing it
awful means dreadful and messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a thing destroyed is broken up, so its letters come out scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Methodist hears the terrible news that Yale has been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are scrambled separately, then one goes round the other; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wesleyans follow John Wesley, founder of Methodism, so the term names a member of that church.

clue.text: Crazy star taking time to make a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, going back the way it came
taking something in means holding it within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the Sun is a star
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A washed-up celebrity takes time out before returning to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SUN to make STUN, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal slang for mad or insane, from the old sense of the head as a nut.
